To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Malaysia and Indonesia have the potential to reduce their CO2 emissions by 20 million tons per year, by 2020, through strategic planning on carbon capture (CC).
Malaysia and Indonesia have the potential to participate in carbon capture projects and to reduce their CO2 emission from existing and future coal-fired power plants.
the coal fired power generation in Malaysia and Indonesia are expected to grow at the rate of 9-10% per year.
In summary, our research is concerned with
strategic planning for the implementation of CC technologies in Malaysia and Indonesia.
the strategic planning for the development of carbon capture from coal-fired power plants in Malaysia and in Indonesia.
the potential and the feasibility for CC from coal fired power stations in Malaysia and Indonesia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the strategic plan for the development of coal fired power plants in Malaysia and in Indonesia should consider CC technology as an option for the reduction of CO2 emission.
the coal fired power plants will continue to play a major role in Malaysia and Indonesia for electricity generation.
the strategic planning for the implementation of carbon capture technology from the existing and future power plants in Malaysia and in Indonesia should be considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coal fired power plant is the major CO2 source and the CO2 capture from the coal fired power plants is the most cost effective way to reduce CO2 emissions in Malaysia and Indonesia.
Malaysia and Indonesia should consider the implementation of carbon capture from existing and future coal based power plants.
the CC technologies have not been fully developed and are still under development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Malaysia and Indonesia have the potential to be the major players in the global carbon market.
the coal consumption in Malaysia and Indonesia will continue to increase, resulting in the increase of CO2 emission from the existing and future power plants.
the coal consumption and CO2 emission in Malaysia and Indonesia will increase significantly in the coming decades.
